Hi Alice,

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through FinLedger's streaming payments demo. As promised, here's a short recap and proposed next steps focused on concurrency and rate limits so we can size Redwood Dedicated or Hosted configuration for your production window.

Recap (from our call)
- Target latency: P95 <= 150 ms per request for 2k-token responses (batching allowed).
- Sustained throughput: ~350 reqs/sec across your three US datacenter regions during peak.
- Burst / peak: up to 1,200 parallel requests for short 45–90s spikes (batching not possible for a subset).
- Streaming: ~60 concurrent streaming sessions (server-to-client streaming) with 20 tokens/sec average per session.
- KV cache hit expected: ~40% on repeated prompts.

Open items for sizing / quota negotiation
1) Connection pooling: you noted the backend will multiplex 8 logical streams per socket. Can you confirm whether your client will keep 8 parallel HTTP/2 streams per TCP connection? That changes recommended connection_pool size from 300 -> ~38 sockets.
2) Retry/backoff behavior: will you enforce client-side exponential backoff (recommended) or expect Redwood to accept queued requests and return 429s?
3) Token accounting: do truncated partial-stream responses count toward your cost budget (we can show illustrations)?

Attached: Redwood_SLO_worksheet.xlsx — fills in our recommended concurrency pool and quota for Hosted vs Dedicated. Also attaching a draft mutual action plan (draft-MAP-Redwood.docx) for timeline and procurement steps.

Next steps proposed
- Can you confirm connection multiplex factor (answer to #1) by EOD Monday?
- We'll follow up with a dedicated engineering note (cc'd Ben & Karthik) that maps your 1,200 parallel-request burst to a connection_pool + socket estimate and a rate-limit policy proposal.
- If numbers look good, we can spin a 2-week trial on Dedicated capacity with reduced commit to validate behavior under real traffic.

If you want a quick call this afternoon to walk through the worksheet I can jump on 30m.

Best,

Thanks — concise recap and exactly what we need. Quick answers inline:
- Multiplexing: yes, our client will open ~50 TCP connections from each of our two edge clusters and use up to 10 HTTP/2 streams per connection for efficiency. So effective multiplex factor is ~10 (not 8).
- Retry/backoff: our platform implements client-side exponential backoff with jitter, but we sometimes push retries aggressively for low-latency flows — we'll need graceful 429s rather than immediate drops.
- Tokens: partial-stream tokens will count toward our cost model; we want to minimize mid-stream truncations.

Priya / Karthik,

Thanks for the ping. Based on Alice's multiplex factor (~10 streams/conn) and their stated peaks I sketched a conservative capacity plan below. I'm attaching a short table to the worksheet (see shared link).

Quick math (conservative):
- Target sustained req/sec: 350 rps -> with 40% KV cache hit effective token throughput reduces ~25% (server-side batching still helps).
- Burst parallel requests: 1,200 requests -> if each connection uses 10 streams that equals ~120 active sockets. Add safety multiplier 1.5 -> 180 sockets.
- Connection pool sizing: for Redwood Dedicated we recommend a connection_pool limit of 200 sockets for FinLedger's primary tenant, with a per-socket stream cap at 12 to provide headroom.
- Throughput quota: suggest initial quota 1,000 rps (protects host from misconfig and allows throttles). We'll present a rate-limit policy mapping: 1,000 rps sustained, 1,500 rps 30s burst window, and token-per-minute ceilings aligned to their cost constraints.
- Streaming: reserve 80 concurrent streaming sessions server-side to avoid head-of-line blocking; token-rate limit 25k tokens/min per tenant as a starting point.

Operational notes:
- Implement a route-level 429 policy that returns Retry-After and a small jitter window.
- Redwood can accept queued requests up to 2x pool size (configurable) but beyond that we return 429. We should confirm FinLedger's tolerance for queued latency vs immediate fail.

I'll prepare a short diagram mapping these numbers to Dedicated pool counts and estimated monthly cost; Priya — can you confirm whether procurement needs a CID (cost-in-detail) or a simple monthly estimate for initial legal review?
